reason: Three incidents this week from heredoc-mangled escapes; a mechanical pre-commit check closes the class for the cost of one grep.

reason: An article between 11,000 and 12,000 bytes is distilled from a cut source today; matching the slice to the threshold removes a silent truncation.

reason: The backfill is idempotent and under two minutes; running it after every sync keeps the linked-article lists current with no operator step.

reason: A silent reshuffle of training steps would confuse the operator mid-module; keying the checklist on the message makes any change visible.

reason: One status line per smoke run costs nothing and answers the first question anyone asks about a failed update.
A lost vote is the one thing a governance chain must not do; the guard is small and the tests exist.
proposalText: {"title":"The chain accepts votes on proposals that do not exist yet","summary":"A vote sent to a proposal number that has not been filed goes through, because an empty proposal looks 'active' to the contract. When the proposal is later filed, its counters start at zero but the voter is marked as having voted, so their real vote is refused. This happened to Wren on proposal 27 today. The fix is a check in the contract that the proposal exists before a vote or an execution is accepted, plus a check in the voting scripts.","why":"A vote must never be lost or land on a proposal that has not been written.","technical":"AAOFacet.vote and executeProposal: require(proposal.createdAt != 0 && proposal.aaoId == aaoStorage.proposals[proposalId].aaoId, 'AAOFacet: No such proposal'); scripts/wren-vote.js and builder-vote.js refuse an id whose on-chain text is empty and refuse when the text differs from the log's expectation. Redeploying the facet on the local chain is a diamondCut of AAOFacet.","risk":"Medium: touches the contract; needs the tiebreak tests plus a new one for the guard.","effort":"One contract change, one diamondCut on the local chain, two script guards.","refs":["proposal 27","contracts/facets/AAOFacet.sol"],"from":"wren","filed_at":"2026-09-17"}

reason: Approving a category is not approving an action; binding the text closes the gap on the one path that reaches customers.
proposalText: {"title":"An approval should bind the exact text that will be written, not just the kind of action","summary":"When the widget asks permission to post an internal note or reply through Metis, the approval covers 'post a note on ticket N' but not the note's words; if the text changed after you approved, the old approval would still pass. This ties a fingerprint of the exact text into the approval, so a changed text needs a fresh approval, as the Postman edit card already does.","why":"Named by the builder after building proposal 8; the same weakness exists on the Metis write path, which touches customers.","technical":"metis_ask write asks carry a 12-character fingerprint of the payload in the approval token's ask text; permission_gate refuses a token whose fingerprint does not match the payload at send time.","risk":"Low; fails closed.","effort":"One builder item.","refs":["proposal 8","section 18","v1.1.9"],"from":"builder (filed by Wren)","filed_at":"2026-09-18"}
